title: Rail Stepper Starter Journey — compact checklist, skeleton empty states, and microtips
creator: Aisha Kaur
design_specs: Accessibility notes: aria-live region, focus outlines, contrast targets
notes: Goal: reduce cognitive load for first-time users by surfacing a minimal horizontal rail stepper with progressive disclosure.
Pattern decision: horizontal rail with compact cards and inline microtips. Trade-off: uses horizontal space but reduces modal churn and step abandonment.
Accessibility: ensure keyboard-only navigation and screen reader announcements (aria-live); contrast >= 4.5:1 for all text states.
Localization: support expanded label lengths for DE/FR/JP; use condensed label tokens and validate with translations before release.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kaur — Created initial proof-of-design with 3 compact card variants and skeleton empty-state assets. Linked Figma and Confluence spec.

2026-03-11 Nina Patel (PM) — Product review: keep a clear 'Skip setup' affordance and request two tone options for microtips (concise vs friendly). Added to labels.
2026-03-12 Mei Chen — Iterated microcopy and spacing; uploaded new hover and focus state screenshots to assets bucket.

2026-03-13 Rafael Gomez (Design Lead) — Approved visual direction pending engineering prototype and accessibility checks.
2026-03-14 Priya Desai (Engineering) — Sync: Eng will prototype with existing component and a11y props. ENG-23345 currently blocked by backend feature flag rollout (ETA 2026-03-20).

approvals: Design lead: Rafael Gomez — visual direction approved 2026-03-13

open_questions: What is the fallback behavior when ENG compactMode cannot be toggled due to older client versions?
Do we expose an analytics event for 'microtip_open' and 'card_dismiss' or rely on existing telemetry?
Should we surface model selection details in the stepper or defer to the model detail view?
risks: Backend flag delay may block prototype integration (ENG-23345).
Localized copy overflow could break compact layout on narrow screens; QA required across languages.
Too many on-rail controls may increase visual noise; aim for maximum of two actions per card.
